newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dragonair orders one additional Airbus A330 plane.
newsitem.headline: Dragonair orders one additional Airbus A330 plane.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie said on Wednesday that Dragonair placed a firm order for an additional A330-300 for delivery in the fourth quarter 1998.
Average price for an A330 twinjet is around $125 million, industry sources said.
The A330 being ordered will be powered by Rolls-Royce Trent 700 engines and will fly major routes between Hong Kong and Beijing, Shanghai, Xiamen and Kaohsiung, Airbus said in a statement.
Hong Kong Dragon Airlines operates an all Airbus fleet.
The A330 will have a two-class layout with 36 seats in first class and 264 in the main cabin.
Dragonair last October ordered two A320 narrow-body jets and placed options for five more.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
